facts.fact: The World Heritage property is a serial group of eight monuments built in the fifth and sixth centuries, not every building in the city.
facts.excerpt: The serial property Early Christian Monuments of Ravenna in north-east Italy consists of eight monuments
facts.location: Readable text capture, exact substring at character 8945

facts.fact: The eight named buildings include San Vitale, Galla Placidia and Sant Apollinare Nuovo; Dante and Piazza del Popolo are not part of that list.
facts.excerpt: the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia, the Neonian Baptistery, the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, the Arian Baptistery, the Archiepiscopal Chapel, the Mausoleum of Theodoric, the Church of San Vitale and the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe
facts.location: Readable text capture, exact substring at character 4192

facts.fact: Ravenna became Western Roman capital in 402, later an Ostrogothic and Byzantine capital.
facts.excerpt: became the capital of the Western Roman Empire in 402 AD, and remained prominent first Ostrogothic and then Byzantine capital in Italy
facts.location: Readable text capture, exact substring at character 9522

facts.fact: UNESCO recognizes both Western and Eastern traditions in San Vitale.
facts.excerpt: combines elements from both the Western and Eastern traditions
facts.location: Readable text capture, exact substring at character 10890

facts.fact: The serial property was inscribed in 1996.
